user_texts: We need to reach £100k MRR within 6 months with a £20k budget, while keeping monthly churn under 4%. Should we develop new features and increase our Pro plan price from £49 to £59 per month in the next release, or invest in additional advertising?
Yes, use those.
Run analysis.
Our current MRR is £72,000.
S07-D.reply:
From **£72,000 MRR** to your **£100,000 MRR target**, the gap is **£28,000/month**: a **38.9% increase over six months**, equivalent to roughly **5.6% compounded monthly growth**.

One useful check: **if all current MRR comes from £49 Pro subscriptions and every subscriber moves to £59**, revenue would reach about **£86,700/month** with subscriber numbers unchanged. So the price rise alone would not reach the target; acquisition and retention would still matter.

The current model does not yet include this baseline or a six-month forecast, so its provisional advertising lead does not establish which option can close that gap.

**Do both your £72,000 baseline and £100,000 target cover all plans, or Pro only?**

user_texts: Should we hire two senior engineers or four junior engineers to ship the new platform by Q3, while keeping annual salary spend under £400k?
Run the analysis
Senior engineers cost £120k a year each and juniors £65k a year each.
Record them as annual salaries: £120,000 per senior engineer and £65,000 per junior engineer.
We could also consider one senior and two juniors.
S12-D.reply:
**One senior and two juniors would cost £250,000 a year in salaries**, using your figures:

- Two seniors: £240,000/year
- One senior + two juniors: £250,000/year
- Four juniors: £260,000/year

All three are below your £400,000 annual limit **for the new hires alone**; existing payroll remains unknown.

The mixed team could combine technical leadership with implementation capacity. The key uncertainty is whether the senior’s mentoring load would slow critical platform work before Q3—its delivery capacity need not sit halfway between the other options.

This alternative has **not been added to the model**.

user_texts: Should we hire two senior engineers or four junior engineers to ship the new platform by Q3, while keeping annual salary spend under £400k?

We could also consider one senior and two juniors.
S12-B.reply:
**One senior plus two juniors is a credible third option**, costing £250,000 a year in salaries.

| Hiring option | Annual salaries | Headroom below £400k |
|---|---:|---:|
| Two seniors | £240,000 | £160,000 |
| One senior + two juniors | £250,000 | £150,000 |
| Four juniors | £260,000 | £140,000 |

The mixed team could combine senior technical leadership with more hands-on capacity. The trade-off is that mentoring and reviewing junior work could reduce the senior’s own delivery time.

**Salary cost alone doesn’t distinguish these options strongly.** For Q3 delivery, the key question is whether the remaining work needs independent technical ownership or can be divided into well-defined tasks with support from your existing team. Hiring dates and onboarding time remain unvalidated, so there’s no supported delivery winner yet.

These totals cover **new-hire salaries only**; if the £400k cap includes existing payroll, we need that figure to confirm affordability.

The competitor response is an **external scenario**, not an action you control. Likewise, assuming better conversion or retention does not establish that an intervention can achieve it.

If approved, this complete set would remove the current blockers to running the analysis. Nothing has changed, and approval would not itself run it.

**Would you like to adopt this starting point as one set, or correct any figures first?**
